newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine banks want dollar sale limit eased.
newsitem.headline: Philippine banks want dollar sale limit eased.

text.p: Philippine banks want the Central Bank to ease limits on over-the-counter dollar sales to $1 million from the current $25,000 per transaction, the Bankers Association of the Philippines (BAP) said.

The association, in a document obtained by Reuters on Wednesday, also said it wanted the government to relax the limit on the volume of transactions in the foreign exchange market to at least 25 percent of banks' unencumbered capital.
It said free trading of swaps between banks with derivatives licenses should be allowed.

The bankers also asked the central bank to simplify registration of foreign exchange investments, to revise settlements for forward and swap transactions and not to require banks to get prior approval before buying dollars from foreign sources.
The limit on the dollar sales of banks promote "underground" transactions, the BAP said.
It also said the Central Bank has to increase the buying and selling limits on foreign currency because the market is now handling large inflows.
